doc.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

title: Mugsy's near-fatal illness and his Ragtime band
summary: His bowel obstruction and long recovery, then the admired Ragtime Band at Nick's with ensemble playing.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: He was going to save my life. He did? Oh yeah, so did he. Normally he touched me. We had Elstram. About an hour from now. Well, I started out with a perforated Elstram. You made his Monsiglo? Obstruction of the bowel. Well, did you know anything about Elstram?
Back in the day, what did you call them? Right?

Well, I think he called them. He called them Ancestral. He knew about him. An obstruction. Veins collapsed. He had 16 transfusions. Low-ver pneumonia. They threw the book at you. Oh sure, I was unconscious for six weeks. No kidding. I was operating on it four times. I didn't even know it. Must have just been hanging on the vine then. Oh, I was. I had low-ver pneumonia too. I was unconscious for about 21 days. Didn't know my way from it. See, the first operation was going to be a good one. They couldn't even move me from the room. They brought the operating room right down to me because they moved me and had been gone. Was it in New Orleans? Yes. I worked two days at the Roosevelt Hotel. Woke up in the hospital. I don't know why I'm here. I don't either. How long did it take you to get over that? I recuperated 18 months. One of my greatest thrills of my life was when you came to New York with your band to Nick's. I was living in Washington, D.C. I came to New York just to hear you. George Zach was still on piano. You know, your first band. Man, that killed me. That was a band. That was a band. That's one of the greatest bands of all time for me. Really. Brunus and Kless. What was his band? Piano player among George Zach. Rode Kless. Rode Kless. That's right. Rode Kless. It was a tight. We used to rehearse like man. I'll tell you, I'd never heard a band like that until then. In person, you know. I'd never heard a band like that. Because that band, they didn't just play solos. You know, now you just hear solos. This band was working with ensembles, ensembles, ensembles.
